summary:
Jonathan Davis suffered a catastrophic crush injury to his left arm when it became entrapped in an industrial stamping press at an NSK plant manufacturing facility. Emergency services responded to find the arm crushed beyond salvage, and he was transported to Midwest Regional Medical Center in traumatic shock with massive blood loss.

Upon arrival, imaging confirmed complete vascular and neurologic disruption with unsalvageable limb damage. The patient underwent emergent above-elbow amputation the same day. He was discharged after a week-long inpatient stay with pain management and referrals for prosthetic evaluation and rehabilitation.

Post-amputation recovery was complicated by severe phantom limb pain and development of a traumatic neuroma at the surgical site, which interfered with prosthetic fitting. He underwent a second surgery several months later to excise the neuroma and reposition the nerve stumps into muscle tissue.

Following neuroma revision, the patient received a custom myoelectric prosthetic arm and completed an extended course of rehabilitation therapy lasting approximately eighteen months. Through this process, his pain progressively resolved from severe to minimal levels. He achieved functional independence with the prosthetic device, including activities of daily living, bilateral coordination tasks, and simulated work-related mechanical activities. He was ultimately discharged from therapy with the ability to return to modified duty work at his employment site.
